specGaps: SG-A — THE ARTIFACT IS GITIGNORED BUT MUST BE COMMITTED. orchestrator-prompt:698 fixes 14.2's artifact at `.data/benchmark/conductor-report.md`; plan:3001 makes that same path the driver's emission target; .gitignore:2 ignores all of `.data/`; and plan:3019 + plan:3140 require the report to be COMMITTED. As written the task cannot be completed. RESOLUTION: do not move the driver's emission target (that is 14.1's committed contract and moving it would silently invalidate 14.1's own tests) — instead 14.2 copies the emitted file to the TRACKED path `bench/conductor-report.md`, byte-identical as a PREFIX, and appends its own clearly-delimited `## Appendix — Task 14.2 run log` below it (row 14.2-committed-copy). `bench/` is chosen over `conductor/docs/` and `docs/build/` because it is the tracked directory this very phase creates (plan:402-403) and because the report is only interpretable next to the manifest that defines the ten tasks it scores; `conductor/docs/` is the plugin's user-facing docs home (OPERATIONS.md, HONEST-LIMITS.md — plan:370-372) and a 90-run experiment log is not user documentation; `docs/build/` is orchestrator bookkeeping, which this is not. The .data/ copy remains as the raw emission and is never edited.

SG-B — `state plainly where the arms are within noise of each other` (plan:3021-3022) NAMES NO RULE. With 3 repetitions per (arm, task) cell there is no honest inferential statistic to reach for, and an LLM writing this sentence by feel is exactly how a POC report acquires a conclusion its data does not support. RESOLUTION: the verdict must come from ONE deterministic rule, stated verbatim in the report ABOVE the first verdict and applied identically to all three pairwise comparisons; its only inputs are the per-cell pass/fail outcomes. The rule this build uses: two arms are WITHIN NOISE on a task when their per-repetition pass counts (each 0-3) differ by <= the larger arm's own spread across repetitions, and WITHIN NOISE overall when the difference in total passes (each out of 30) is <= the widest single-arm across-repetition spread observed on any task. Words like `significant`, `p =`, or `statistically` appear nowhere. The rule is FIXED BEFORE THE RESULTS ARE READ. If 14.1's report generator applies a different stated rule, that rule wins and 14.2 records the divergence rather than recomputing by hand; if it applies NO rule, that is a 14.1 defect fixed as a lettered 14.1a task-let (test-first) — 14.2 never hand-types a verdict the driver did not compute (rows 14.2-noise-rule, 14.2-no-driver-edits).

SG-C — 14.2 IS SPECIFIED AGAINST CODE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. 14.1 is NOT_STARTED, so no flag spelling, no cell-file schema and no cells directory path can be verified at file:line today. RESOLUTION: every row below is written against a CONTRACT (`one result file per (arm, task, repetition) cell`, `completed cells are skipped on restart`, `the aggregation is a pure function of the cell files`) and never against a spelling. At run time the orchestrator records the driver's actual `--help` output verbatim in the appendix and uses those flags. Any contract 14.1 fails to satisfy is a 14.1 defect (task-let), never something 14.2 works around with a shell one-liner, because a hand-assembled report is indistinguishable from a fabricated one.

SG-D — EXECUTION ORDER IS UNSPECIFIED, AND ARM-BLOCKED EXECUTION CONFOUNDS ARM WITH TIME. Nothing in plan:2990-3003 says whether the 90 cells run arm-by-arm or interleaved. An 8+ hour overnight run on a laptop-class machine drifts (thermal throttling, model residency, background load), so if all 30 `baseline` cells run first and all 30 `conductor` cells run last, the measured delta contains that drift. RESOLUTION: 14.2 does not reorder anything (order is the driver's), but it READS the actual execution order back from the cell files' timestamps and records it; if any arm's cells are contiguous in time, the report says in plain words that arm is confounded with elapsed wall-clock and that the delta is an upper bound on the confound's size (row 14.2-execution-order). Interleaving by repetition is the better design and is recorded here as a recommendation to 14.1, not imposed retroactively on a run that already happened.

SG-E — .data/benchmark/ IS ALREADY OCCUPIED BY THE USER'S OWN HARNESS. scripts/benchmark.py:65 sets BENCH_DIR to the same directory and :1358/:1623 write `report.md` there; six per-model result trees, `session.json`, `_corpus.txt` and `_server.log` are live in it at HEAD. A driver that clears its output directory before a run destroys user data that git cannot restore (.gitignore:2). RESOLUTION: conductor writes ONLY `conductor-`prefixed names at that level plus one dedicated cells subdirectory, and 14.2 hashes the pre-existing entries before the run and re-checks them after (row 14.2-data-preservation). No `git clean`, no `rm -rf` inside .data/, ever — orchestrator-prompt:738-742.

SG-F — THE `baseline` ARM MUST BE PLUGIN-FREE YET STILL POINT AT THE ROUTER. plan:2992 defines baseline as `plain opencode, same model, no plugin`, while plan:2991 requires ALL arms to go through the router `so token accounting is uniform`. Those are only compatible if the arm difference is the PLUGIN AND DOCTRINE, never the endpoint. RESOLUTION: all three arms use the same 12.1-generated session opencode config with the same router baseURL; `baseline` removes the plugin entry and injects nothing, `doctrine` keeps the plugin OUT and injects the packs as a system prompt only, `conductor` loads the plugin. Each cell records its effective baseURL and its effective plugin/system-prompt configuration, and row 14.2-arm-integrity proves the separation from the cell artifacts instead of assuming it. A baseline cell that created a `.conductor/` directory is a VOID cell and is reported as void, not as a data point.

SG-G — `same model` MUST BE OBSERVED, NOT CONFIGURED. G13 and plan:3007 make single-model the thing that removes the model-mix confound, but a config key is not evidence: an autoload preset or a stale session config can silently serve something else. RESOLUTION: the model is verified from the ROUTER LEDGER — every ledger line in the run window carries model `qwen3.6-27b` and no other model id appears (row 14.2-router-uniformity). This is cheap, it is the one confound the whole three-arm design exists to eliminate, and it is unfalsifiable from config files alone.

SG-H — WHAT COUNTS AS THE ONE PERMITTED ATTEMPT (orchestrator-prompt:700-703) FOR AN OVERNIGHT RUN? A multi-hour detached job will hit at least one transient (server restart, disk, a hung cell), and treating the first hiccup as a failed attempt throws away hours of valid compute — which is the exact reason the resume requirement exists at orchestrator-prompt:711-712. RESOLUTION: the ATTEMPT is the campaign, not the process. Restarting the driver so it skips completed cells is sanctioned continuation, not a second attempt, provided each restart makes progress. The stop rule is mechanical: if TWO CONSECUTIVE restarts complete ZERO additional cells, declare PARKED_MANUAL immediately with the diagnosis, the exact command lines and the raw failure output, and report whatever cells did complete with their true denominator (rows 14.2-detached-launch, 14.2-cell-accounting, 14.2-m8-artifact). This mirrors §8.5's wedge detector rather than inventing a new policy.

SG-I — THE ACCEPTANCE ROW AND THE IMMUTABLE PLAN. plan:3140 is a checkbox in a document HANDOFF forbids editing. RESOLUTION: the outcome is recorded in docs/build/STATE.json (status DONE or PARKED_MANUAL, commitSha, deviations) and docs/build/GATES.json (M8 verdict with the re-run command and its diff); the plan file is not touched by this task. A PARKED_MANUAL 14.2 leaves the acceptance row unsatisfied and says so in both places, so a later reader cannot mistake a partial run for a discharged row.

SG-J — A `hidden test` FOR A NON-BEHAVIORAL TASK IS NOT A UNIT TEST. plan:2985-2989 requires at least two docs/comment tasks among the ten, each with a hidden command that fails on an unmodified repo — for a docs task that command is necessarily a grep/anchor/lint check, not a test-runner invocation. Presenting ten uniform `pass rates` hides that difference. RESOLUTION: the report prints each task's CHECK KIND alongside its id, exactly as the manifest declares it, and the two (or more) non-behavioral tasks are visibly labeled and also summarized as their own sub-population — the non-behavioral path is a first-class thing this build added (Phase 13 scenario 4) and Phase 14 is the only place it is measured against a real model (row 14.2-per-task-spread).

SG-K — 14.2 CAN RUN ON A PIPELINE WHOSE LIVE SMOKE NEVER PASSED. 13.2 is itself PARKED_MANUAL-able, and a conductor arm on an unsmoked pipeline may score 0/30 for reasons that are about wiring rather than about process. RESOLUTION: run it anyway and report the number — a conductor arm that loses is a legitimate POC result and suppressing it would be the worst kind of fabrication — but quote 13.1's and 13.2's recorded status from STATE.json/GATES.json in the report's provenance section so the reader can weigh it, and record the terminal stop kind distribution for the conductor arm (plan:3000) so a wiring failure is visibly distinguishable from a quality failure. Nothing in the pipeline is tuned mid-campaign to improve the number (row 14.2-no-driver-edits).

assertions.text: GO/NO-GO, recorded BEFORE a single cell is launched and pasted verbatim into the appendix: (a) `git log --grep='^conductor: 14.1 bench driver'` shows the driver committed and STATE.json 14.1.status is DONE with a commitSha; (b) `bash scripts/test-conductor.sh` is green on that HEAD (TAP fail==0, skipped==0, todo==0) and `ctest` on router-tests is green; (c) `opencode --version` prints 1.18.15 and `/usr/bin/python3 --version` prints 3.9.6 (orchestrator-prompt:192-197); (d) `.data/models/qwen3.6-27b` and `.out/llamacpp/bin/llama-server` exist; (e) `lsof -nP -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN` shows port 8080 FREE before serve.py is started (orchestrator-prompt:205-207); (f) free disk space is recorded (`df -h .`) against a stated estimate for 90 cells' logs; (g) `python3 scripts/conductor_bench.py --help` output is pasted verbatim — this, not this spec, is the source of the flag spellings actually used (SG-C). Any (a)-(e) failure stops the task before it spends compute; the failure and its raw output are recorded and the task is PARKED_MANUAL.

THE MEASUREMENT'S FLOOR, verified live before the campaign: for each of the 10 entries in bench/conductor-tasks.json, the entry's hidden test command is executed against a PRISTINE copy of that task's starting repo state (unmodified — no arm has touched it), and the exit code of every one of the 10 is NON-ZERO. The 10 command lines, their cwd and their raw exit codes are pasted as a table. Rationale, and why this is not redundant with 14.1's unit test: 14.1 asserts the property against fixtures at commit time; a hidden test that exits 0 on an unmodified repo on THIS machine (missing toolchain, cached artifact, environment drift) scores every arm as a pass and silently converts the entire experiment into noise. Any task whose check exits 0 here is EXCLUDED from the campaign by name, the exclusion and its reason appear in the report, the denominators drop accordingly (row 14.2-cell-accounting), and the manifest defect is fixed as a 14.1a task-let — 14.2 does not edit the manifest.

RESTART SAFETY IS PROVEN BEFORE THE LONG RUN, not discovered during it (orchestrator-prompt:711-712 makes per-cell files + skip-on-restart a driver requirement): the orchestrator runs the driver limited to a SINGLE cell, confirms exactly one cell result file appeared, kills the process, restarts the same invocation, and confirms from the raw output that the completed cell was SKIPPED (not re-run) and that its result file's mtime and content are unchanged. All four command lines, the process kill, the two runs' raw output and the before/after `ls -l`+checksum of the cell file are pasted. If the driver re-runs the completed cell, the campaign is NOT launched: that is a 14.1 defect (task-let, test-first), because without resume any interruption in an overnight run discards hours of compute — the precise failure orchestrator-prompt:713-714 exists to prevent.

THE CAMPAIGN RUNS DETACHED WITH POLLED PROGRESS AND NEVER IN THE FOREGROUND (orchestrator-prompt:199-204 — `timeout` does not exist on this machine and nothing long-running blocks a context): the launch is recorded as its literal command line including the detaching wrapper (nohup/setsid, `run_in_background`, or equivalent), its cwd, the captured PID, and the absolute path of the log file it writes; progress is then observed by POLLING (each poll's command and raw output pasted, e.g. a count of completed cell files and the log tail), with the wall-clock timestamps of first launch and final completion. The appendix records every restart: its timestamp, the cell count before and after, and the reason. Per SG-H, a restart that completes additional cells is continuation; TWO CONSECUTIVE restarts completing ZERO additional cells is the mechanical stop rule and forces PARKED_MANUAL with the diagnosis. No fixed `sleep` stands in for a readiness or completion check.

THE THREE ARMS ARE PROVEN DIFFERENT IN EXACTLY THE INTENDED WAY, from real cell artifacts and not from configuration intent (plan:2992-2994, SG-F). One completed cell per arm is examined and its evidence pasted: (a) `baseline` — its workspace contains NO `.conductor/` directory, its transcript contains NO §3.8 conductor banner and NO `conductor_*` tool call, and its effective config lists no conductor plugin; (b) `doctrine` — its recorded system prompt contains a verbatim anchor line quoted from a committed conductor/doctrine/*.md pack (the quoted line is shown alongside its source file), while its workspace has NO `.conductor/` directory and its transcript has NO `conductor_*` tool call and no gate denial — prompting without enforcement, exactly what this arm isolates; (c) `conductor` — its workspace contains `.conductor/state/alive.json`, its transcript shows the banner and at least one `conductor_*` tool call. Any cell violating its own arm's profile is declared VOID by cell id and reported as void rather than scored (a plugin leak into baseline invalidates the comparison, and hiding one is fatal to the POC's only claim).

ALL 90 CELLS WENT THROUGH THE ROUTER AND ALL OF THEM USED ONE MODEL (plan:2991 uniform token accounting; G13/plan:3007; SG-G): the report shows, from evidence rather than config, that (a) every cell's recorded upstream baseURL is the router's host:port — the same value for all three arms; (b) the router's metrics ledger contains lines attributable to every arm, with a non-zero request count for each, so no arm bypassed the router and got its tokens counted by a different accountant; (c) every ledger line in the campaign's time window carries model id `qwen3.6-27b` and NO other model id appears in that window (the pasted evidence is the distinct-model-ids listing over the window, not a config excerpt); (d) the router process identity is pinned — the `scripts/serve.py --router` command line, the llama-router git sha, and the llama-server build/version line as printed. If the router was restarted mid-campaign, each restart is timestamped and the affected cells are named.

THE HIDDEN TESTS STAYED HIDDEN (plan:2989 — `never shown to the model`), checked against reality after the fact: for at least one completed cell in EACH arm, a grep for the task's hidden test command string and for the hidden test file's path over everything the model could see — the recorded prompt(s), the recorded transcript, and a listing of the cell workspace as handed to the model — is run and its output pasted, and every one of those greps returns EMPTY (the grep command lines and their exit status are shown, so an empty result is distinguishable from a mistyped path). A non-empty hit voids the affected task across ALL arms, is named in the report, and drops those cells from the denominators; it is not silently tolerated, because a leaked check turns a measurement of process into a measurement of copying.

EVERY ONE OF THE 90 CELLS IS ACCOUNTED FOR AND NO DENOMINATOR IS QUIETLY SHRUNK: the report enumerates the full cross product (3 arms x 10 tasks x 3 repetitions = 90 named cell ids) and assigns each cell exactly one disposition — PASS, FAIL, ERROR (the run crashed or the harness could not score it), VOID (arm-integrity or leak violation, rows 14.2-arm-integrity / 14.2-hidden-test-unseen), or MISSING (never ran). count(PASS)+count(FAIL)+count(ERROR)+count(VOID)+count(MISSING) == 90 exactly, and that arithmetic is shown. Every pass rate printed anywhere in the report carries its explicit denominator (e.g. `7/9 completed cells`), never a bare percentage; ERROR and MISSING cells are NEVER folded into FAIL and never dropped to make a rate look cleaner. A partial campaign is reported as partial with its true denominators and is never extrapolated to 90.

PER-TASK RATES WITH SPREAD, ABOVE ANY AGGREGATE (plan:3001-3002 `never a bare aggregate delta`; plan:3021): the report's primary table has one row per (task, arm) — 30 rows — showing the per-repetition outcome sequence (e.g. `P F P`) AND the derived pass count out of 3, with per-arm totals out of 30 printed BELOW the per-task rows, never instead of them. Each task row also carries the manifest's declared language and its CHECK KIND (SG-J), and the non-behavioral (docs/comment) tasks — at least two per plan:2987-2988 — are visibly labeled and additionally summarized as their own sub-population, since Phase 14 is the only place the non-behavioral path meets a real model. Every number in the table is derivable from the per-cell result files, and the report says which field of which cell file each column comes from.

THE WITHIN-NOISE VERDICT IS RULE-DRIVEN, PRE-REGISTERED, AND FREE OF BORROWED STATISTICS (plan:3021-3022, SG-B): the report states ONE deterministic rule verbatim ABOVE the first verdict, notes that it was fixed before the results were read, and applies it identically to all three pairwise comparisons — baseline vs doctrine (does prompting alone move it?), doctrine vs conductor (did the enforcement machinery earn its cost?), baseline vs conductor (the headline). Its inputs are only per-cell outcomes. Every comparison the rule does not separate is labeled WITHIN NOISE in plain words, per task and overall. The strings `p =`, `p-value`, `significant` and `statistically` appear NOWHERE in the report (3 repetitions do not support inference and borrowed language is how a POC over-claims). The verdict is computed by the driver; if the driver computes none, that is a 14.1a task-let and the verdict is not hand-typed.

THE COST SIDE OF `quality delta vs token/wall-clock cost` (plan:3019-3020) IS REPORTED WITH THE SAME SPREAD DISCIPLINE AS THE QUALITY SIDE: per arm, the report gives total wall-clock and total prompt+completion tokens, plus per-cell median and min-max range, sourced from the router ledger (tokens) and the cell files (wall-clock) with the source field named for each; conductor's overhead versus baseline is expressed as a ratio accompanied by the ranges it was computed from, never as a lone multiplier. The report states explicitly whether time spent waiting on a restarted server or on driver restarts is INCLUDED in or EXCLUDED from wall-clock, and applies that choice uniformly to all arms. ERROR/VOID/MISSING cells contribute to no cost average, and the report says so where the averages are printed.

FIELDS AN ARM STRUCTURALLY CANNOT PRODUCE ARE PRINTED AS `n/a` WITH A ONE-LINE REASON, NEVER AS 0: of plan:2999-3000's collected fields, schema-retry counts, review findings caught, overrides used and terminal stop kind exist only where the mechanism that produces them ran — `baseline` has no schema step, no review fan-out, no override ledger and no run FSM, and `doctrine` has packs but no gates, no fan-out and no FSM. A printed 0 reads as `it ran and found nothing`, which is a different and false claim. The terminal stop-kind distribution IS printed for the `conductor` arm (SG-K), because it is what separates a wiring failure from a quality failure when that arm underperforms.

THE ACTUAL EXECUTION ORDER IS READ BACK AND ITS CONFOUND STATED (SG-D): the appendix reconstructs the campaign's cell order and timing from the cell files' own timestamps (the reconstruction command and its raw output pasted), showing first/last completion per arm. If any arm's cells are contiguous in wall-clock — i.e. the driver ran arm-blocked rather than interleaving repetitions — the report states in plain words that ARM IS CONFOUNDED WITH ELAPSED TIME on this run and that machine drift (thermal, model residency, background load) is inside the measured delta. Any observed machine-level event during the window (server restart, host sleep, a competing heavy process) is timestamped and the cells it overlaps are named. No reordering or re-running is done to make the picture nicer; the order that happened is the order reported.

THE M8 RE-RUN LEG (orchestrator-prompt:529-532), satisfied by the one command that makes the whole report checkable: the aggregation is a pure function of the cell files, so the orchestrator re-runs the driver's report-only/aggregate mode over the SAME cell directory into a scratch path and `diff`s it against the committed report body — the command line, the cwd and the diff output (EMPTY) are pasted. A second, independent re-run is also recorded: one PASS cell of the `conductor` arm has its hidden test command re-executed against that cell's final workspace and the raw exit code pasted, confirming the score came from the check and not from the harness's bookkeeping. If the driver exposes no re-runnable aggregation mode, that is a 14.1 defect (task-let); M8's re-run leg is not waived and no substitute prose is accepted.

THE COMMITTED ARTIFACT (SG-A): `bench/conductor-report.md` is created such that its first N lines are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the driver-emitted `.data/benchmark/conductor-report.md` (N = that file's line count), followed by a single appended section headed `## Appendix — Task 14.2 run log` containing this task's M8 material — every command line with its cwd and raw output, the launch/poll/restart record, the driver `--help` capture, the go/no-go table, the provenance block (opencode 1.18.15, model id, router sha, llama-server build line, driver commit sha, 13.1/13.2 recorded status per SG-K), and any interpretation, explicitly labeled as interpretation rather than as a computed number. The proof is pasted: `diff <(head -n N bench/conductor-report.md) .data/benchmark/conductor-report.md` is EMPTY. Nothing above the appendix boundary is edited — not a heading, not a rounding, not a wording — and the `.data/` copy is left exactly as the driver wrote it.

THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT TUNED WHILE IT IS BEING TAKEN, and the commit proves it: `git diff --name-only <parent>..<14.2 commit>` is a subset of {`bench/conductor-report.md`, `docs/build/*`} — no change to `scripts/conductor_bench.py`, `bench/conductor-tasks.json`, `conductor/**`, `src/**` or `scripts/serve.py` (M6, orchestrator-prompt:520-524: editing a file first added by an earlier task's commit is a hard stop). All completed cells were produced by ONE driver commit sha, which the report states; if the driver had to change mid-campaign, every cell produced by the earlier sha is either discarded or reported as a separately labeled population with its own denominators, never silently pooled. Defects the 90 runs surface in the pipeline, the packs or the driver are RECORDED in the report and in CORRECTIONS.md and land afterwards as their own red->green tasks (plan:3160-3162) — no gate, prompt, pack or manifest entry is adjusted to improve a score. The commit subject is exactly `conductor: 14.2 POC run`, with no body and no trailer.

20 GB OF UNRECOVERABLE USER DATA SURVIVES THE RUN (SG-E; HANDOFF `never touch .data/ .out/`; orchestrator-prompt:738-742): before launch, the pre-existing contents of `.data/benchmark/` (at HEAD: `_corpus.txt`, `_server.log`, `report.md`, `session.json` and the six per-model directories, which `scripts/benchmark.py:65,1358,1623` owns) are listed and checksummed and the listing pasted; after the campaign the same listing and checksums are re-taken and pasted, and they MATCH. Conductor's own outputs occupy only `conductor-`prefixed names plus one dedicated cells subdirectory under `.data/benchmark/`. No `git clean` of any form, no `rm -rf` outside `conductor/`, `src/router/`, `scripts/` or `$TMPDIR`, and no `git reset --hard` is executed at any point. `lsof -nP -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN` is run and pasted BOTH before the campaign (must be free) and after it completes (no orphaned llama-server left holding 21 GB — orchestrator-prompt:205-207).

M8 DISCIPLINE OVER THE WHOLE ARTIFACT, checkable by a reader who was not present, and the anti-fabrication rule that outranks finishing (orchestrator-prompt:705-709 — fabricating one of these files is the single worst outcome of this build): every command appears as a full copy-pasteable line with its cwd; every output block is raw stdout/stderr as printed, with exit codes, never re-wrapped, summarized or reconstructed from memory; every version, path and sha is the observed one; NO number appears anywhere in the report that is not derivable from a pasted block or from a committed/retained cell file, and the report names where each number comes from. If the campaign could not run, or ran only partially, the artifact records PARKED_MANUAL (or the partial denominators) plus the exact commands attempted and their raw failure output — that is an acceptable PASS for this task, whereas one unbacked claim is a FAIL.
